facts.text: Lakeside was founded in 1886 when 6,600 acres around Lindo Lake were bought by the El Cajon Valley Land Company, which built an 80‑room Victorian inn.
The town’s name comes from the small natural lake that originally surrounded the settlement, but today it hosts three large reservoirs: Jennings, El Capitan, and San Vicente.
A trailhead in Lakeside leads up to the summit of El Cajon Mountain, locally nicknamed “El Capitan” for its resemblance to the famous Yosemite cliff.
Lakeside earned a reputation as a cowboy town, featuring an 8‑acre rodeo ground that still hosts events and supports local youth through the El Capitan Stadium Association.
All three reservoirs in Lakeside are stocked by the California Department of Fish and Wildlife with bass, catfish, and rainbow trout, drawing anglers from the region.
Geographically, Lakeside sits in the western foothills of the Cuyamaca Mountains, giving it a mild climate and scenic backdrops for outdoor activities.
